about: Each entry pairs a 2026 duty with the 2016 duty it replaces. text_2016 and text_2026 are plain-language summaries written in matching wording, so a word-by-word comparison shows real differences and not differences in phrasing. 2016 facts come from published summaries of the 2016 Rules (NIUA/ICLEI slides, the NPC toolkit and the CAG summary); 2026 facts come from the gazette PDF. Verify against the gazette before relying on any line.

pairs.text_2016: Every waste generator must segregate and store waste in three separate streams: bio-degradable, non-bio-degradable and domestic hazardous waste, and hand it to authorised waste pickers or collectors.
pairs.text_2026: Every waste generator must segregate and store waste in four separate streams: wet, dry, sanitary and special care waste, and hand it to authorised waste pickers or collectors.
pairs.what_changed: Three streams became four. Sanitary waste now has its own stream, wet and dry replace the bio-degradable and non-bio-degradable names, and 'special care' replaces 'domestic hazardous' (the examples are similar: bulbs, batteries, medicines).

pairs.text_2016: Used sanitary waste such as diapers and sanitary pads must be wrapped securely and put in the bin meant for dry waste.
pairs.text_2026: Used sanitary waste such as diapers and sanitary pads must be wrapped securely and put in the separate bin meant for sanitary waste.
pairs.what_changed: Sanitary waste leaves the dry-waste bin and gets its own sanitary-waste bin.

pairs.text_2016: A waste generator must not throw, burn or bury solid waste on streets, in open public spaces or in drains.
pairs.text_2026: A waste generator must not throw, burn or bury solid waste on streets, in open public spaces or in drains.
pairs.what_changed: Same duty in both versions. The exact wording of the clauses differs slightly; read the full 2026 clause below.

pairs.text_2016: A waste generator must pay the user fee for solid waste management that the local body's bye-laws specify.
pairs.text_2026: A waste generator must pay the user fee for solid waste management that the local body's bye-laws specify.
pairs.what_changed: Same duty in both versions. The amount is not in the Rules: it comes from the local body's bye-laws.

pairs.topic: Housing societies, hotels and other large premises
pairs.text_2016: Resident welfare and market associations, hotels, restaurants, gated communities and institutions above 5,000 sq m must ensure source segregation, hand recyclables to authorised collectors, process wet waste on the premises by composting or bio-methanation as far as possible, and give residual waste to the local body's agency.
pairs.text_2026: Resident welfare and market associations, hotels, restaurants, gated communities and institutions above 5,000 sq m must ensure source segregation, hand recyclables to authorised collectors, process wet waste on the premises by composting or bio-methanation as far as possible, and give residual waste to the local body's agency within one year of notification of the Rules.
pairs.what_changed: The list of premises and duties is the same. The 2026 clause carries a one-year deadline from notification; I did not check whether the 2016 clauses had one.

pairs.topic: Bulk waste generators: registration and returns
pairs.text_2026: Every bulk waste generator must register on the centralised online portal with the local body and file an annual return by 30 June each year.
pairs.what_changed: New in 2026. The 2016 summaries I used describe bulk generators only as partners of the local body; they have no portal registration or annual return.

pairs.text_2016: Local bodies must paint bins for bio-degradable waste green, bins for recyclable waste white and bins for other waste black.
pairs.text_2026: Local bodies must paint bins for wet waste green, bins for dry waste blue and, optionally in public toilets, bins for sanitary waste red.
pairs.what_changed: Blue replaces white for dry waste, black disappears, and red bins for sanitary waste appear (optional, in public toilets).

pairs.text_2016: Local bodies must arrange door-to-door collection of segregated waste from all households, including slums and informal settlements, and from commercial, institutional and other non-residential premises.
pairs.text_2026: Local bodies must arrange door-to-door collection of segregated waste from all households, including slums and informal settlements, and from commercial, institutional and other non-residential premises.

pairs.text_2016: Local bodies must frame bye-laws that incorporate the provisions of the Rules within one year of the Rules coming into force.
pairs.text_2026: Local bodies must frame bye-laws that incorporate the provisions of the Rules by 31 March 2027.
pairs.what_changed: Same duty with a new deadline: a fixed date (31 March 2027) instead of one year from the 2016 notification.

pairs.text_2016: Industrial units within 100 km of a refuse-derived-fuel plant must replace at least 5% of their solid fuel with RDF within six months of the Rules coming into force.
pairs.text_2026: Industrial units within 100 km of a refuse-derived-fuel plant must replace at least 6% of their solid fuel with RDF from the start, rising to 10% after 3 years and 15% after 6 years.
pairs.what_changed: The target rises from 5% to 6% and then steps up to 10% and 15%. The six-month start-up window is replaced by 'from the start'.

pairs.text_2016: District magistrates must review the performance of local bodies every quarter.
pairs.text_2026: District magistrates must review the compliance of local bodies at least once every quarter and upload the minutes of the review meeting on the local body's portal.
pairs.what_changed: The quarterly review stays. The minutes must now be uploaded on the portal.

pairs.text_2016: Operators of processing facilities must send an annual report (Form III) by 30 April.
pairs.text_2026: Operators of processing facilities must file quarterly returns by the 15th of the first month of the next quarter and an annual return (Form III) by 30 June.
pairs.what_changed: Quarterly returns are new and the annual deadline moves from 30 April to 30 June. The 2016 date comes from the NPC toolkit summary.
